ca_3_iron_curtain.blurb: Iron Curtain is a steep wall on the Table Rock cliff, in the Palisades above Calistoga in the northeast Bay Area wine country. It holds 12 routes, nearly all of them bolted sport lines plus a single trad climb. Most of the grades sit around 5.11, with a pair of 5.8s at the easy end and one 5.12 at the top. The face is covered in pockets, cobbles and ripples, and it feels noticeably steeper than it appears from the slope below, so expect sustained pulling rather than a casual outing. The hillside angle makes the lines hard to read from the ground. Rock here can be soft in places.

ca_stirrup_rock_north_face.blurb: The north side of Stirrup Rock is a compact, shady face in the Pinto Basin part of Joshua Tree National Park, on a dark-patinated granite formation. There are 12 routes, mostly trad with two bolted lines and one top-rope. Grades run from an easy 5.6 up through the 5.12 range, with a good handful in the 5.10s and 5.11s, so it suits moderate leaders as well as people looking for a stiffer fight. Because it faces away from the sun it is a sensible choice when the park heats up, and it tends to be quiet. The walk from the parking area is short and flat.
ca_stirrup_rock_north_face.approach: A short, level walk of about five minutes from the parking area to the large brown formation, then around its end to the north side. No boulder hopping.

ca_sports_challenge_rock_east_face.blurb: This is the east side of Sports Challenge Rock, the big central formation in Real Hidden Valley, Joshua Tree National Park. The 12 routes are mostly trad with three top-rope lines, and the stone is dark and solid. The wall leans toward steep and overhanging, so the climbing is powerful and the grades are stiff: one easy-looking 5.9 start, a few 5.10s, then the bulk of the routes between 5.11 and 5.12. The trail from the south splits at the formation, with the right-hand branch leading here. A little easy scrambling gets you to the base of some lines. Good for strong climbers wanting short, hard single pitches.

ca_upper_tier_11.blurb: Upper Tier is the higher of two ledges at North End, a moderate sport and trad cliff in Rock Creek, in the eastern Sierra above Mammoth Lakes. It has 12 single-pitch routes of roughly 100 to 150 feet on granite that is mostly solid, with technical face and slab climbing and some steeper steps. Most grades fall in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, with a single easier line, which makes it friendly for newer leaders. Bring a mix of trad gear and quickdraws. The cliff sits at high elevation, so expect summer sun, cool evenings, and snow that limits the season to late spring through early fall.

ca_puppy_dome.blurb: Puppy Dome is one of the smallest domes in Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite National Park, standing right beside the road with only a short stroll to its base. It has about a dozen routes, mostly trad with a couple of boulder problems. The gentle, low-angle side offers easy introductory climbs, while the far side steepens into an overhanging wall with the harder, better-quality lines, up to the 5.13 range. Between those extremes there are routes across the middle grades. Walkers can also scramble the slabs for the summit view over the meadows toward Tioga Pass and Cathedral Peak. A convenient spot for a quick session or a first Tuolumne day.
ca_puppy_dome.approach: A short walk of about five minutes from the road and parking area; the dome is close by and in plain view.
